steps.tx: **Basal cell carcinoma** BCC is the most common human cancer, driven by aberrant constitutive activation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway through PTCH1 loss-of-function or SMO activating mutations. PTCH1 encodes a transmembrane receptor that normally represses smoothened SMO. Pathogenic inactivation of PTCH1 releases SMO from tonic inhibition, promoting GLI1 and GLI2 nuclear transcription factor translocation that orchestrates malignant basaloid proliferation.

steps.tx: Oral targeted agents provide non-surgical options for locally invasive or metastatic lesions. **Hedgehog pathway inhibitors** vismodegib and sonidegib bind smoothened SMO to achieve high objective response rates in locally advanced or metastatic basal cell carcinoma. In the ERIVANCE trial, vismodegib demonstrated an objective response rate of forty-three percent in locally advanced disease, with class-related toxicities including muscle spasms, alopecia, dysgeusia, and weight loss.

left.title: Vismodegib (ERIVANCE Trial)
points: Binds SMO receptor drug-binding pocket
Approved for locally advanced and metastatic BCC
43% ORR in locally advanced, 30% in metastatic
Common toxicities: muscle spasms, dysgeusia, alopecia

right.title: Sonidegib (BOLT Trial)
points: Selective oral SMO antagonist
Approved specifically for locally advanced BCC
Tissue distribution with long half-life
Monitored for creatine kinase elevation and rhabdomyolysis

steps.tx: Extensive cumulative ultraviolet solar damage induces substantial neoantigen loads in cutaneous tumours. **Cutaneous squamous cell** carcinoma cSCC carries high ultraviolet radiation mutational burden, responding robustly to anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibodies cemiplimab and pembrolizumab. In the EMPOWER-CSCC 1 trial, cemiplimab induced an objective response rate of forty-seven percent with prolonged durability in patients with locally advanced or metastatic cSCC ineligible for curative surgery or radiotherapy.

rows: 47% ORR; first FDA/EMA approval in advanced cSCC
50% ORR in locally advanced, durable disease control

steps.tx: Primary cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinomas exhibit aggressive locoregional and distant spread. **Merkel cell carcinoma** MCC is an aggressive cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma driven by Merkel cell polyomavirus MCPyV integration in 80% of European/US cases or chronic UV damage. Tumours express characteristic paranuclear dot-like cytokeratin 20 CK20 and neuroendocrine markers chromogranin and synaptophysin, but lack thyroid transcription factor 1 TTF-1, distinguishing MCC from metastatic small cell lung cancer.

left.title: MCPyV-Positive Merkel Cell Carcinoma
points: Clonal integration of Merkel cell polyomavirus
Expression of Small T and Large T antigens
Low somatic mutation burden
Commoner in European and North American populations

right.title: UV-Driven Merkel Cell Carcinoma
points: Virus-negative etiology
Extremely high ultraviolet mutational signature
Frequent TP53 and RB1 mutations
High tumor mutational burden and neoantigen load

steps.tx: The micrograph shows blue tumour cells with tiny brown dots beside each nucleus, the classic paranuclear dot like pattern. This **Merkel cell carcinoma** is an aggressive skin neuroendocrine cancer linked to polyomavirus or sun damage. It stains for **CK20** plus chromogranin and synaptophysin while **TTF1** stays negative. That profile separates it from small cell lung cancer and confirms the diagnosis.
steps.say: This stain clinches Merkel cell carcinoma. Look for small blue tumour cells with brown paranuclear dots of CK20, plus neuroendocrine markers chromogranin and synaptophysin. TTF1 negativity is the key negative that points away from small cell lung cancer spread to skin. For exams, link the dot like CK20 pattern to Merkel cell carcinoma and recall its aggressive spread and viral or sun driven origin.

vis.alt: The micrograph shows blue Merkel tumour cells with brown paranuclear dot like CK20 staining.
vis.caption: CK20 dot like staining confirms Merkel cell carcinoma. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Immune checkpoint blockade provides definitive durable disease control in metastatic cutaneous neuroendocrine tumours. **Avelumab** anti-PD-L1 antibody induces rapid, durable objective responses in chemotherapy-refractory and treatment-naive metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma in the JAVELIN Merkel 200 trial. Responses were durable, with over seventy percent of responses lasting twelve months or longer, establishing front-line anti-PD-L1 monotherapy over cytotoxic chemotherapy.

steps.tx: Congenital DNA repair defects dramatically accentuate ultraviolet skin carcinogenesis. **Xeroderma pigmentosum** XP is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by defective nucleotide excision repair NER, conferring a 10000-fold increased risk of developing skin malignancies. Inability to excise cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers and 6-4 photoproducts leads to multiple early basal cell carcinomas, squamous cell carcinomas, and melanomas in childhood, mandating strict UV avoidance.

edges: UV-signature CC to TT transition mutations

steps.tx: Constitutive germline Hedgehog pathway aberrations manifest with multiorgan developmental and neoplastic lesions. **Gorlin syndrome** nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome is caused by germline PTCH1 mutations, predisposing to dozens or hundreds of basal cell carcinomas, odontogenic keratocysts, and medulloblastomas. Skeletal abnormalities include bifid ribs, calcification of the falx cerebri, and palmar and plantar pits. Therapeutic radiation must be strictly avoided.

steps.tx: Precise histological margin control guarantees maximal cosmetic preservation and cure. **Mohs micrographic surgery** provides the highest cure rates for high-risk facial basal cell and squamous cell carcinomas by microscopically examining 100% of surgical margins intraoperatively. Fresh tissue is excised, mapped, frozen, and sectioned horizontally, allowing complete visualization of peripheral and deep margins while sparing critical healthy periorbital, nasal, and labial architecture.

left.title: Mohs Micrographic Surgery
points: Horizontal frozen sections inspect 100% of margin
Highest cure rate (>99% primary, 95% recurrent)
Preserves maximum normal functional tissue
Indicated for high-risk facial 'H-zone' tumors

right.title: Standard Bread-Loafing Excision
points: Vertical sections evaluate <1% to 2% of margin
Standard 4 to 6 mm surgical margins required
Potential for false-negative margin assessment
Suitable for low-risk trunk and extremity lesions

steps.tx: Four panels trace nasal **Mohs micrographic surgery** from saucer shaped layer removal to colour coded mapping of quadrants one to four. Microscopy shows horizontal **frozen section** review with tracked margins and full peripheral plus deep **margin evaluation**, then targeted re excision of the involved focus. The sequence matters because complete margin review gives the highest cure while sparing nearby normal nose tissue and appearance.
steps.say: The top left shows a thin saucer of skin lifted from the side of the nose. The top right maps the sample into four colour zones so any involved edge can be traced back to its exact site. The bottom left shows frozen section microscopy checking the whole outer and deep edge, and the bottom right removes only the remaining focus. By checking every edge during surgery, this method clears high risk facial tumours while saving healthy tissue.

vis.alt: The four panel sequence shows nasal layer excision with colour mapping plus microscopy and targeted re excision.
vis.caption: Four panel sequence shows mapped excision with microscopy guiding targeted re excision, Illustration: StewardMD original.
